paper.title: Self-organized pinning and interface growth in a random medium

headline: Sneppen 1992 interface depinning (model A, CA disclosed): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; chi=0.65 (in [0.5,0.75]), avalanches span 5.0 decades (max/median 30968x), adjacent-slope corr=+0.26

verdicts.gate: P1 self-affine: W_sat(L)~L^chi with chi in [0.5,0.75] AND W_sat monotone in L
P2 scale-free avalanches: span >= 2.0 decades AND max >= 100.0x median nonzero
P3 anticorrelated growth: adjacent interface-slope correlation < 0
reasons: adjacent-slope correlation = +0.2603 (need < 0; a self-affine Sneppen interface has POSITIVELY correlated adjacent slopes — a rising region keeps rising — so this clause is falsified); random-deposition baseline = -0.4709

extra.framing_detail: extremal-dynamics SOC model — one advance selects the GLOBAL minimum-pinning column and raises it, then enforces a bounded-slope constraint on its neighbours; centralized / model-orchestrated, not agent-stepping (no scheduler over an agent roster, no per-agent perceive/decide/act), disclosed exactly as the BTW-sandpile and Bak-Sneppen reproductions are
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + lock-first discipline reproduce the Sneppen self-affine roughening (roughness exponent chi), scale-free extremal-avalanche activity, and the interface geometry, and would catch an artifact

citations: Sneppen, K. (1992). Self-organized pinning and interface growth in a random medium. Physical Review Letters 69(24):3539-3542. doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.3539.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the Sneppen depinning signatures (roughness exponent chi, scale-free avalanche tail, adjacent-slope correlation), with a random-deposition slope-correlation baseline reported as an internal contrast
